title: WhoIs called per-request with no cache — correct security posture for revocation
description: kith-tslocal/src/lib.rs opens a fresh Unix socket connection for every WhoIs call. This means a peer revoked from the tailnet is rejected on the next request, with only the in-flight request window (~5s timeout) as exposure. A future contributor might add caching for performance. Caching WhoIs results creates a revocation window (a removed peer retains access until cache TTL expires). The per-request cost is a local Unix socket round-trip — negligible. Do not cache WhoIs.
